concepts.label: XDCR Reference (registered target cluster)
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - this is the concept's own defining page. 'A _reference_ is the registration, on the local cluster, of details that identify a target cluster for XDCR replication.' First contact anywhere in the corpus for the reference-registration object itself, as opposed to the settings/filtering mechanisms the xdcr-reference/ tree (round 20) documents. Genuinely UI-procedure-only vocabulary: the reference tree never needed to name the act of registering a target cluster, because it assumes one already exists.

concepts.label: Full Admin / Full Administrator (Server RBAC role)
concepts.reused_or_minted: reused - as the source-side administrator role required to set up the reference

concepts.label: XDCR Inbound (target-cluster receiving role)
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - a target-side role, granted to the credential a reference authenticates with, that permits one or more buckets to RECEIVE documents from an incoming XDCR replication. Structurally distinct from the source-side Full/Cluster/XDCR Administrator roles that gate MANAGING XDCR: this one gates being a valid replication destination. server/8.0/learn/security/roles.json's own notable_absence explicitly lists 'XDCR Inbound' among roles deliberately NOT extracted from roles.md in that batch ('per the brief's explicit instruction to extract selectively rather than mechanically') - so this is this role's first full extraction anywhere in the corpus, discovered exactly where the brief predicted admin-procedure-only vocabulary would surface.

notable_absence.finding: The page states a genuine integrity constraint - 'if a reference is already associated with a replication, you cannot delete the reference; nor can you modify its target IP address' - that this registry has no clean predicate for: cascadesTo/cascadesDeletionTo describe deletion PROPAGATING, not being BLOCKED. Rather than force this onto an ill-fitting predicate or mint a new one for a single occurrence, the fact is recorded here in prose and as a cascadesTo relation on the weaker (edit-propagation) half of the same sentence, which does fit cleanly.

cross_component_finding: THE 'XDCR INBOUND' ROLE IS A CLEAN CONFIRMATION OF THIS BATCH'S SIDE-BY-SIDE-READING INSTRUCTION. server/8.0/learn/security/roles.json (a sibling round-26 batch, not round 20's reference tree) explicitly listed 'XDCR Inbound' among roles it deliberately did NOT extract, naming it by name in its own notable_absence field. This page is the first in the corpus to actually put that named-but-unextracted role into a real access-control relation - the kind of gap only visible by reading roles.json's own margin notes against this batch's procedure pages.
